name: Raw carrot salad (Ray Peat)
lead: The raw carrot salad is a daily food habit associated with the bioenergetic diet popularised by the American biologist Ray Peat. It is typically a shredded raw carrot dressed with a little oil, vinegar and salt, eaten as a side dish. Followers in Peat-influenced forums describe it as a gut-and-hormone routine that they connect to clearer skin, a calmer complexion and a leaner, less puffy look.

Peat's followers say the carrot's fibre keeps the intestine tidy by moving along bacterial endotoxin and surplus estrogen, which in their account lets the skin, hair and body composition look better over time. Raw carrot is also a source of fibre and beta-carotene, the pigment that gives some people a warmer skin tone when carotenoid intake is high.
No clinical trial has tested the carrot salad protocol as Peat's followers describe it.

chain: Fibre and carotenoids reach the gut and skin
Clearer, warmer-looking complexion as described by followers
angle.text: Followers eat a shredded raw carrot with oil and vinegar each day, reasoning that it supports gut and hormone balance and in turn skin clarity and a leaner look. Carotenoid-rich foods are also discussed for a warmer skin tone.

infobox: Shredded raw carrot, oil, vinegar, salt

paras: The salad is a small portion of raw carrot, often grated or cut into thin strips, dressed with a modest amount of oil (coconut or olive oil are commonly named), a splash of vinegar and some salt. Peat-diet communities treat it as a staple alongside foods such as orange juice, milk and cooked mushrooms.

Proponents say the insoluble fibre in raw carrot binds or speeds the clearance of estrogen and gut endotoxin, reducing what they regard as a drag on thyroid function and skin quality. Users report smoother skin, less bloating and a sharper facial outline.
No studies found. General research on dietary fibre and on carotenoid intake and skin colour exists, but those studies are of broader categories and did not test this salad.
Very high carotenoid intake can give the skin a yellow-orange tint (carotenemia), which is harmless and fades when intake falls. Raw fibre can cause gas or loose stools in people unaccustomed to it.

card.summary: A daily dressed raw carrot that Ray Peat followers eat for gut, hormone and skin benefits.
card.note: Very high carotene intake can tint skin orange.

quick.overview:
The raw carrot salad is a shredded carrot with oil, vinegar and salt, eaten daily by followers of Ray Peat's bioenergetic diet.

People use it hoping for clearer skin, less bloating and a leaner look, and many simply enjoy it as an inexpensive side dish.
quick.mechanism: Followers say carrot fibre helps carry endotoxin and excess estrogen out of the gut, which they link to better skin and body composition. Carrots also supply fibre and carotenoids that can warm skin tone.
quick.risks: Generally a low-risk food. Large amounts of carotenoids may tint the skin orange, and raw fibre can cause gas in some people. No clinical trial has tested the protocol.
